novel_features.name: Clinical Queries refinement
novel_features.description: Refine a clinical or disease topic to therapy, diagnosis, etiology, prognosis, clinical-prediction, or systematic-review evidence, with open-access, evidence-level, and human/language/age scope filters.
novel_features.rationale: Reproduces PubMed's Clinical Queries by layering the canonical Haynes filter strategies onto esearch — no incumbent CLI exposes this as a first-class command.
novel_features.why_it_matters: When a clinician or agent needs evidence of a specific type on a disease topic, this returns the right slice without hand-crafting filter syntax.

novel_features.name: Article cards in one call
novel_features.description: Search and return clean article cards (title, authors, journal, date, DOI, PMID, evidence-level badge, optional abstract) with open-access and clinical scope filters, in one command.
novel_features.rationale: Collapses esearch + esummary + optional efetch into one widget-ready JSON payload, tags each result's evidence level from its publication types, and applies open-access/human/language/age filters inline.
novel_features.why_it_matters: The dashboard widget calls one command and renders ranked, evidence-tagged cards — no client-side orchestration of E-utilities.

novel_features.name: Abstract by PMID
novel_features.description: Fetch one or more abstracts by PMID as clean structured JSON or plain text.
novel_features.rationale: efetch returns only XML/MEDLINE upstream; this parses it into structured JSON the API never emits directly.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Gives an agent the abstract text for a known PMID in one clean call, no XML parsing.

novel_features.name: Publication trend
novel_features.description: Publication counts per year (or month) for a topic, ready to chart.
novel_features.rationale: Fans esearch across date buckets and aggregates locally; E-utilities has no trend endpoint.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Gives the dashboard a time-series of research attention on any disease or intervention.

novel_features.name: What's new since last check
novel_features.description: Return only articles new since the last run of a saved query, using a local seen-PMID store.
novel_features.rationale: Requires persisting seen PMIDs per query in a local store — impossible with a stateless API wrapper.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Powers a live 'new research' panel and disease-surveillance alerts without re-showing seen results.

novel_features.name: Saved queries
novel_features.description: Persist named queries with their filters, re-run them, and see when each last ran.
novel_features.rationale: Local store of named searches — the substrate for watch and trend on recurring topics.
novel_features.example: pubmed-pp-cli saved add af-anticoag "atrial fibrillation AND anticoagulation" --json
novel_features.why_it_matters: The widget can drive a fixed panel of standing clinical questions by name.

novel_features.name: Topic landscape
novel_features.description: Facet a query's top results by journal, author, year, or evidence level to show where the literature concentrates.
novel_features.rationale: Local aggregation over the fetched result set — no single E-utilities call returns these rollups.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Surfaces the leading journals/authors on a disease topic for at-a-glance dashboard context.

novel_features.name: PICO clinical question builder
novel_features.description: Compose a structured Patient/Intervention/Comparison/Outcome question into a precise PubMed query and run it.
novel_features.rationale: Encodes evidence-based-medicine question structure into query translation — a clinical workflow no wrapper models.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Lets a clinician or agent ask a well-formed evidence question and get the matching literature directly.

novel_features.name: Two-term co-occurrence lens
novel_features.description: Track how often two terms (e.g. a drug and an adverse effect, or a disease and an intervention) appear together in the literature over time.
novel_features.rationale: Fans esearch across term A, term B, and 'A AND B' per year and computes co-occurrence locally — no single E-utilities call returns an association series.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Surfaces emerging drug-safety or disease-intervention signals as a time series for the dashboard.

narrative.headline: Every PubMed E-utility, plus clinical-query refinement, a local article store, and trend/what's-new analytics no other PubMed tool ships.
narrative.value_prop: pubmed-pp-cli wraps NCBI E-utilities with agent-native JSON on every command, then adds a clinical-evidence layer (clinical, pico), widget-ready article cards (find), and a local SQLite store that powers trend, watch (what's new), and topic landscape. Built for dashboards and agents, not Unix one-liners.

quickstart.comment: confirm the tool is wired and E-utilities is reachable
clean article cards for a topic in one call
publication counts per year for a chart

troubleshoots.fix: Set NCBI_API_KEY to raise the limit from 3 to 10 requests/sec; the CLI adds it automatically when present.
efetch has no JSON mode upstream; use 'find --with-abstract' or 'abstract <pmid>' for clean JSON, or 'fetch get' for the raw record.
Use --scope broad for a sensitive search; --scope narrow maximizes specificity and intentionally returns fewer, higher-precision hits.

narrative.when_to_use: Reach for pubmed-pp-cli when an agent or dashboard needs biomedical literature: clinically refined evidence on a disease or intervention, clean article metadata for a query, publication trends, or a 'what's new' feed on a standing topic. It returns structured JSON built for programmatic consumption.
anti_triggers: Do not use it to retrieve full-text article PDFs — E-utilities returns metadata and abstracts, not licensed full text (use the PMC links it surfaces).
Do not use it for non-PubMed databases beyond what Entrez exposes; it is scoped to PubMed literature.
Do not use it as a citation manager of record — export to BibTeX/RIS and manage citations in a dedicated tool.
